newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI says to bring banks' CRR below 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI says to bring banks' CRR below 10 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intends to lower the cash reserve ratio (CRR) of banks to 10 percent and below, the central bank governor said on Monday.
"The objective will be to take the CRR to 10 percent and below," Chakravarty Rangarajan said while addressing a meeting of bank economists at the western Indian town of Mahabaleshwar.
"We are already on this path and the effective CRR has come down from 15.7 percent at the end of March 1995 to 11.5 percent in June 1996," he said.
Changes announced in October 1996 would bring down the effective CRR to below 10 percent, he said.

Unveiling the credit and monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) in October 1996, Rangarajan had announced a two percentage point cut in CRR in four instalments of fifty basis points each.
The first two have already taken place and the next two are scheduled to take effect in January 1997.
Rangarajan said the statutory liquidity ratio had also been brought down to an effective rate of 27.5 percent in March 1996 from from a mid-1991 peak of 37.5 percent.
